group.passage:
The Selfridges in London is famed as one of the best department stores in the world. Proudly standing on prestigious Oxford street, this huge establishment boasts high-end merchandise of a wondrous variety. Luxurious beauty hall, sprawling shoe gallery, pampering spa, and even an in-store psychic—Selfridges has something for everyone. [[1]]
Perhaps lesser-known is the fact that it was founded by an American. Born in Ripon, Wisconsin, in 1858, Harry Gordon Selfridge started working at a dry-goods store at the age of 12. [[2]] A young and fun-loving boy, Selfridge quickly noticed how people viewed shopping as a chore. They came to the counter, specified their order, paid and left. He envisioned a store where merchandise was on display so that customers could look at it and touch it, where shopping could be enjoyable.
Following a trip to London, Selfridge invested a large sum of money to build a new department store in the then unfashionable western end of London. The Selfridges was open to the public in 1909. [[3]] The perfume counter, for example, was placed at the eye-catching spot on the main floor. Sales papers and advertisement flyers were posted and distributed. From the 1920s to 1930s, there was even a gun club for women on the top floor. [[4]] Today, Selfridges continue to thrive as one of London’s most iconic department stores. Perhaps not as famous or popular among foreign tourists as Harrods, Selfridges is definitely a place visitors to London mustn’t miss.

options_bank.A: That is, as long as they have money to spare.
options_bank.B: During World War II, the basement served as an air-raid shelter.
options_bank.C: Back then, people did most of their shopping in stores like this.
options_bank.D: It revolutionized shopping, and boasted lots of “firsts” among its peers.
